# Look up a code through Bloom filter, cache and DynamoDB

> `resolve` turns a short code into a live link by checking its format, a Bloom filter, a cache and then DynamoDB, and it returns nothing for unknown or expired codes.

_Part of [Creating and resolving share links](share-short-links.md)_

When someone opens `GET /l/:code`, the service calls `resolve` in [`ShareLinkService`](link-click-analytics.md). It first checks the code looks right: 4 to 32 letters, digits or dashes. Anything else gets `null` right away, with no lookups. Next it asks the Bloom filter ([`RedisBloomFilter`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/infrastructure/cache/bloom-filter.ts#L12), a compact Redis set that can say "definitely not a code" or "maybe") about the code. If the answer is "definitely not", `resolve` returns `null` and stops. That way, people scanning random codes never reach the cache or the database. If Redis fails, the check is treated as "maybe", so real links still work. Codes are added to the filter in `create` after they are saved. For "maybe" codes, `resolve` calls the cache helper `getOrLoad`, which loads the link from the `Links` DynamoDB table on a miss. Misses are cached for a short time too, so a repeated bad code doesn't hit DynamoDB each time. At the end, a link whose expiry time has passed is dropped and `null` is returned. The caller turns `null` into a 404. See [Creating and resolving share links](share-short-links.md) for the full create and redirect flow.

**Look at:** [`resolve` in share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts#L41) · [`RedisBloomFilter` in share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts#L9)

## Pieces

- Cheap format check on the code: A regex lets only 4 to 32 letters, digits and dashes through, so junk never touches Redis or DynamoDB.
- [Bloom filter that rejects codes that never existed](bloom-filter-gate.md): `mightContain` on a Redis-backed Bloom filter (sized for 100 million codes at a 1% false-positive rate) returns `null` for unknown codes and lets everything through if Redis errors.
- [Cache lookup that also remembers missing links](cache-with-negative-caching.md): `getOrLoad` keeps a link under `link:v1:<code>` for 1 hour, serves stale data for up to 24 hours while refreshing, and remembers "not found" for 60 seconds.
- Loading the link from DynamoDB: On a cache miss, a `GetCommand` reads the item by `code` from the `Links` table, or gives `null` if it's not there.
- Dropping links that have expired: If the link's `expiresAtEpoch` (expiry time in Unix seconds) is in the past, `resolve` returns `null` as if the link did not exist.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| cache | `share-links:bloom` | Redis Bloom filter that `resolve` reads with `mightContain` and `create` writes with `add`. |
| cache | `link:v1:<code>` | Cached link, or a cached "not found", via `getOrLoad`; `create` invalidates it so a newly claimed alias isn't shadowed by an old miss. |
| database | `Links` | DynamoDB table read by `code` with `GetCommand` when the cache has no answer. |

## Also relies on

- [Creating and resolving share links](share-short-links.md): `resolve` is the lookup step of the share-link redirect, and `create` fills the Bloom filter and the table it reads.

## Watch out

- A Bloom filter can say "maybe" for a code that doesn't exist (about 1% of the time), so the cache and DynamoDB still have to say 404.
- If the Bloom filter call fails, `resolve` treats the code as possibly real, so a Redis outage means more cache and DynamoDB lookups, not failed redirects.
- A missing code is cached for only 60 seconds, so `create` invalidates the cache key to stop a freshly created custom alias from looking missing.
- Expired links are only dropped when read. They stay in DynamoDB and the Bloom filter, and a cached copy can still be served until `resolve` checks the expiry.
